newsitem.title: UK: Taiwan agreement on new Hong Kong flag seen soon.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan agreement on new Hong Kong flag seen soon.

text.p: The chairman and president of Hong Kong-based shipping giant World-Wide Shipping Group, Helmut Sohmen said the colony's handover to Chinese rule would involve a smooth transition for its shipping register.
"The only change to the autonomous Hong Kong shipping register will be the need to change the flag flown on the ships," he said last night in a speech in London.
Hong Kong-registered vessels will fly two flags following handover of the colony to China on July 1, 1997 - the Chinese national flag and the new Hong Kong flag, Sohmen said.
However, there is still a questionmark over Taiwan allowing ships flying the Chinese flag to enter its ports.
Sohmen said: "Negotiations are currently under way."
Observers believe an agreement allowing ships flying the new Hong Kong flag access to Taiwanese ports, and vessels registered in Taiwan entry to Hong Kong could be ready as soon as April.
Sohmen indicated that he believed an agreement was close, and said both sides were being "very realistic."
"There are no signs that owners are looking to change register overnight. Most believe that the register will remain its current size - that is around 15th largest in the world," he added.
Around 8m tonnes is physically registered in Hong Kong, he said.

Direct shipping links between China and Taiwan have been banned since 1949 when the Communists came to power on the mainland. Attempts over recent years to set up links between the two countries have foundered on political tensions.
Sohmen was speaking at a lecture to the Company of World Traders at the Guildhall in London before news of the death of China's leader Deng Xiaoping broke.
